The Concept

Sound that rises.
Light that breaks.

The Ascension is a worship concert — but the brief was bigger than a concert poster. It needed to feel like a moment. Like the air before the first note.

The visual language is built around radiant light bursting from a central figure — Joshua Obafemi mid-cry, eyes closed, mic raised. Behind him, light rays explode outward in copper and peach, the warm glow of something sacred breaking through.

The system was designed to scale across an entire campaign — from the headliner's solo poster, to the full ensemble lineup, to a six-day countdown series — without ever losing the central feeling: ascension as a sensation, not a slogan.

"Every poster in the campaign feels like the same moment, captured from a different angle."

The Headliner

Joshua
Obafemi.

Lead Minister · Headliner

The campaign's central image — Joshua mid-worship, captured at the peak of a note. The poster system makes him the focal point of every primary asset, with the supporting artists (Steve Hills, Paul Tomisin, David Smile) introduced through their own dedicated pieces beneath the same visual language.

Guest Minister Series

Three artists.
One visual world.

Each guest minister received their own dedicated poster within the same system — Joshua silhouetted at the top, the wordmark wrapping around them, the featured artist taking centre stage below. Same campaign, different focal point.

Countdown Series

Six days.
One build-up.

A daily countdown sequence designed for social rollout — from "5 Days To Go" through to "Today". Each piece reuses the same campaign system but flips the hierarchy: the day count becomes the dominant visual, the wordmark recedes to a header role.

Cream and Peach form the light core — the centre of every burst, the place the eye lands first. Soft, warm, almost devotional in their quality.

Copper carries the campaign's warmth outward, anchored by deep Ink — the void from which the light breaks. The palette feels like a sunrise captured mid-bloom.
